title: The Static of the Kuiper Line
premise: Tamsin Ishikawa, a clone of the murdered detective whose unsolved case she inherited, has spent twelve years hauling cargo through the contested Kuiper Line, hiding her identity behind forged registries. When the derelict freighter Halcyon Wake returns from deep space with its crew aged backward into children, Tamsin is the only pilot both desperate and deniable enough to board it, and she finds the ship's logs contain a message from the original Tamsin — proof that the war's founding atrocity was staged by the Admiralty itself. Pursued by the naval officer she loves and the intelligence service that made her, Tamsin must choose between delivering the message that will end the war and destroying it to protect the found family of misfits who have become her crew. In the reactor countdown's final minutes, she broadcasts the truth to both fleets, exposing the conspiracy at the cost of her ship, her anonymity, and nearly her life; the war ends not with victory but with mutual recognition, and Tamsin finally claims her own name instead of her original's ghost.
about_author: Coral Ravensworth is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years writing technical manuals for deep-space freight contracts before turning to fiction. She lives in a coastal town where she repairs radios, collects failed mission transcripts, and insists the best science fiction begins with paperwork gone wrong.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Quiet
chapters.summary: Tamsin Ishikawa hauls contraband seed stock through the Kuiper Line checkpoint at Ceres Gate, dodging an Admiralty scan by hiding inside a decommissioned ore barge. Her POV establishes her forged registry, her loneliness, and the murder case file she keeps encrypted under her bunk. Emotional beat: competent isolation — she has built a life designed to leave no trace.

chapters.title: The Ship That Came Home Young
chapters.summary: Dockworkers flag the freighter Halcyon Wake drifting into port with no transponder history; when Tamsin helps tow it in, they find the crew alive but aged backward into children who remember being adults. Salvage law makes the ship hers if she claims salvage rights. Emotional beat: dread mixed with temptation — the wreck is a trap or a gift.

chapters.title: Children Who Remember Dying
chapters.summary: In the Halcyon Wake's medbay, Tamsin interviews the child-crew and learns their voyage lasted forty subjective years through a fold anomaly. One girl, Sefa, recognizes Tamsin's face and calls her by her original's name: Detective Ishikawa. Emotional beat: uncanny grief — Tamsin confronts how much of her identity was never hers.

chapters.title: The Case File Opens Itself
chapters.summary: The ship's black box contains a sealed message addressed to 'the second Tamsin,' keyed to her clone genome. Inside: coordinates, a partial recording, and evidence that the Kuiper Line war began with a massacre that never happened. POV shifts briefly to the original Tamsin via log entries. Emotional beat: inheritance becomes obligation.

chapters.title: Crew of the Unwanted
chapters.summary: Tamsin assembles her ragtag crew: disgraced medic Oyelaran, ex-fleet gunner Brask, and stowaway engineer twins Vex and Mio. She tells them enough of the truth to sign on, lying about the rest. The children are left with a harbor matron Tamsin trusts. Emotional beat: found family forming around shared secrets.

chapters.title: Lieutenant Vale
chapters.summary: Admiralty Lieutenant Idris Vale boards Tamsin's ship for a routine inspection and finds the black box's empty cradle. He covers for her — he has loved her since the Ceres blockade years ago — but reports the anomaly anyway. Dual tension between duty and feeling. Emotional beat: love as liability on both sides.

chapters.title: Fold Coordinates
chapters.summary: Following the message's coordinates, the crew navigates a debris field littered with ships from both fleets, all decades old, all officially lost. They realize both sides have been erasing the same region of space. Emotional beat: mounting horror — the war's history is a curated lie.

chapters.title: What the Anomaly Shows
chapters.summary: At the fold threshold, the ship's instruments record time running backward in thin sheets. Oyelaran theorizes the anomaly reverses biological age along exposure gradients — explaining the children. Tamsin realizes someone deliberately flew the Halcyon Wake into it. Emotional beat: scientific awe curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: The Massacre That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Inside the fold, they find the passenger liner Meridian intact, undamaged, holding ten thousand empty evacuation pods — the 'massacre' that justified twelve years of war was a staged disappearance. Brask, whose brother died in the war's first battle, breaks down. Emotional beat: betrayal at civilizational scale.

chapters.title: Intercepted
chapters.summary: An Admiralty hunter-kill squadron corners them at the fold mouth; Vale is aboard and orders them to surrender the black box. Tamsin plays one minute of the Meridian recording over open channels, and two escort captains hesitate. Emotional beat: the truth as a weapon that cuts both ways.

chapters.title: Vale's Choice
chapters.summary: Vale boards under truce, sees the liner with his own eyes, and must decide between his oath and Tamsin. His superior, Admiral Corvane, arrives with orders to destroy the site and everyone who witnessed it. Emotional beat: duty cracking against love and conscience.

chapters.title: Corvane's War
chapters.summary: POV chapter from Admiral Corvane: she knows the truth — she helped stage the Meridian — because ending the war required a cause worth dying for, and peace had made both fleets politically expendable. She is not a monster; she is a true believer. Emotional beat: chilling sympathy for the antagonist.

chapters.title: Running the Fold
chapters.summary: Tamsin takes the ship into the anomaly itself to escape Corvane's guns, gambling that the fold will shield them. The passage ages the hull decades in minutes; Vex and Mio keep the reactor patched while reality stutters around them. Emotional beat: terror and wonder fused — flying through unmade time.

chapters.title: The Message Completed
chapters.summary: Deep in the fold, the black box unlocks fully: the original Tamsin's final recording reveals she found the Meridian first, was silenced for it, and cloned herself deliberately so the evidence would outlive her. Tamsin hears her original ask forgiveness for the burden. Emotional beat: reconciliation with the self she was made from.

chapters.title: Sefa's Warning
chapters.summary: A signal reaches them from the harbor matron: Corvane's agents have taken the child-crew as leverage. Sefa smuggles out a coded distress using memories only the real crew would know. Emotional beat: protective fury — the family Tamsin built is now the hostage.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Truth
chapters.summary: Tamsin devises the endgame: broadcast the full Meridian evidence simultaneously to both fleets' open channels so neither command can suppress it. But transmission requires the relay array at Ceres Gate, which means flying back through Corvane's blockade. Emotional beat: resolve hardening into sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Countdown Begins
chapters.summary: Corvane, cornered, arms the fleet's scorched-earth protocol: a reactor detonation seeded in Ceres Gate's core that will destroy the relay and the station, blaming Tamsin's 'terrorist cell.' The countdown gives the finale its clock. Emotional beat: dread with a deadline.

chapters.title: Blockade Run
chapters.summary: The crew threads the blockade in the dying ore barge, Vale feeding them gaps in the patrol grid from inside Corvane's flagship until he is caught. Brask takes the helm when Tamsin is wounded; the twins vent the cargo to make burn mass. Emotional beat: every member of the found family spending themselves for the others.

chapters.title: Reactor Zero
chapters.summary: Tamsin reaches the relay core as the countdown hits double digits; she must physically splice the broadcast into the array while Corvane's saboteurs close in. She sends the truth — and a personal appeal in her original's voice, asking both fleets to stand down. Emotional beat: climax — one woman's voice against a war machine.

chapters.title: Stand Down
chapters.summary: Across both fleets, ships hold fire as the Meridian evidence spreads through every channel; escort captains refuse Corvane's final order, and Vale, escaped custody, arrests her with her own bridge officers' consent. The reactor is vented with ninety seconds left. Emotional beat: catharsis — the war ends not in battle but in refusal.

chapters.title: Aftermath of a Name
chapters.summary: Weeks later, tribunals begin and the child-crew of the Halcyon Wake grow forward again under guardianship. Tamsin, legally dead twice over, is offered a new identity by both governments; instead she registers under her own chosen name, neither the original's nor a forgery. Emotional beat: claiming selfhood at last.

chapters.title: The Static Clears
chapters.summary: Tamsin and Vale take a small ship back to the fold's edge, where the anomaly is quietly collapsing, and release the original Tamsin's ashes into the current. The crew signs on for one more run together — not cargo this time, but the first civilian survey of the Liner Meridian. Emotional beat: belonging earned, love chosen, the future open.
